reason: The cave is central to both goals, so checking what can be used there should clarify where to start.
expectation: The inspection should reveal which available items can interact with the cave.

effect: The cave's only available interaction produced an echo, suggesting a route toward the song. The correction also shows that Call is no longer available.
reaction: The reflected voice is a fitting starting point for separate voices.
reason: The social group might respond to the echo together, though this is a guess.
expectation: The group may turn the echo into a shared vocal activity.

effect: Echo did not combine with the group, but the compatibility feedback automatically combined it with Memory to make Song.
reaction: The remembered and altered echo is a satisfying route to song, though I had guessed the wrong partner.
reason: Earth and water might make a pigment or paint for the cave wall.
expectation: Mixing earth and water may produce a material for painting.

effect: Earth and water made pigment, but it still needs a painter.
reaction: The material is a clear first step toward the cave image.
reason: The social group could use the pigment to make an image.
expectation: The group may begin painting with the pigment.

effect: Pigment cannot combine directly with the group; the cave is its available partner.
reaction: The feedback makes the painting route clear.
reason: Use the pigment at the cave to make a mark on its walls.
expectation: The pigment will produce a cave image or a step toward one.

effect: Pigment and Memory at the cave created a cave painting, bringing the image goal closer.
reaction: The remembered image makes sense as a starting point for painting.
reason: Combining the painting with a story may turn the image into an imagined creature.
expectation: The story may give the painting an impossible subject.

effect: The story transformed the cave painting into an imagined beast, completing the creature goal and revealing a new goal about colouring a sky.
reaction: Combining familiar parts into an unseen creature is a compelling example of the makers inventing something new.
reason: The starfield is the clearest starting point for a sky, but its role in colouring one is not yet clear.
expectation: The inspection should reveal what can be combined with the starfield to make their own sky.

effect: The starfield inspection automatically used pigment in the cave to create a painted sky, completing the new goal.
reaction: An imagined sky fits the theme of the makers creating beyond observation.
reason: The remaining goal calls for separate voices, so the social group is a plausible partner for Song.
expectation: The group may turn the song into a shared performance with separate voices.

effect: Song and Social group made a chorus, completing the last goal and the chapter.
reaction: The emphasis on listening between separate voices is a fitting conclusion.

mostWorthwhile.text: Turning the cave painting and a story into an imagined beast was most worthwhile: familiar memories became something the world's inhabitants invented for themselves.

leastWorthwhile.text: Trying to give pigment directly to the social group was less rewarding; the feedback simply redirected me to the cave.

surprise.text: Inspecting the starfield immediately created a painted sky using pigment at the cave. I expected compatibility information, not the completed image.

arbitrary.text: Using memory with an echo to make a song was not obvious beforehand, although the result explained how a remembered phrase could be altered and repeated.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see what else the inhabitants create independently, especially after the imagined beast and chorus.
